Independent judgment: APPROVE, and on the BRIEF's direction question, PROCEED. This is a genuinely minimal, pre-admission delivery-only repair that closes no scientific finding and launches no model (model_calls:0 across the final-context preflight and installer postchecks).

(1) Context-overflow fix is representational only. The sole production behavior change is in manual_context.workspace_artifact: nine exact existing item4 configuration IDs (current-reviewed-notebook-selection, item4-current-backlog-selection, item4-operator-document-1..5, spec-size-guidance, provenance-guidance) now route to the existing hash-bound read-only workspace-file delivery, but only when private_intake is not None. For those IDs build() now emits only the descriptor (path+sha256) inline and writes raw bytes to a 0o400 file (lines 229-240), instead of decoding raw inline (line 242). Every selected row's raw still passes git_publication.scan at line 228 before delivery, so the privacy gate is not bypassed by the relocation. All open obligations, STATE, POLICY and operator docs remain verbatim inline via budget.assemble; the 200000-char bound (measure/check_final) and dispatch_preflight stop/flagged gates run before _workspace_files materialization, so a stop, secret or oversize aborts before any file is written. test_item4_review7_delivery confirms exact-byte 0o400 delivery with raw absent from body, path+sha present, body<200000, and refusals (changed/missing/symlink/private/oversize) leaving no workspace/evidence. Evidence shows the composed input dropping from 206782 (ORIGINAL_PREFLIGHT_FAILURE) to 198066 (ACTUAL_FINAL_CONTEXT), consistent with moving ~9 config artifacts out of the inline CURRENT ARTIFACTS section.

(2) No approval-path regression. The second caller experiment_approval.inspect (line 97) omits private_intake, but its required_rows are only REQUIRED[item] types plus the configuration ids frozen-execution-plan and authored-execution-plan; none of the nine new ids appear there. For frozen-execution-plan the config branch evaluates false both before and after the change (it is not in the unconditional set), so it stays inline exactly as before. The asymmetry is therefore inert on that path.

(3) Grant identity is correctly preserved. load()/continue_review6()/run() switch the continuation approval from v['review_sha256'] to held_third_continuation_approval(). Because this install makes REVIEW_CHANGE=item4-review7-context-delivery, after install v['review_sha256'] would be the review7-delivery approval hash, not the original author12/review7 grant. held_third_continuation_approval pins THIRD_SOURCE=c1a712bc.. and THIRD_REVIEW=d1b610.. and verifies verdict==APPROVE, change_id==item4-review6-continuation-20261008, matching PRIOR_APPROVED_REPORT.json. granted() in the continuation module compares the previously stored grant event's review_sha256 against this approval, so the switch is required to keep the stored (12,7) grant valid; it adds no new allowance. scope() still admits only {(10,5),(11,6),(12,7)}; terminal_transition still maps the final review to stop-code 4 (no author13/review8).

(4) Installer and accounting are consistent. The prior-source gate moves SECOND->THIRD, correctly requiring the currently installed review6-continuation helper, and the reconciliation check now asserts phase run_spec_review, rounds author:12/review:6, 18 manual_calls and validator v3 -- exactly the post-author12 lane state.
